purpose: Practise reading the WHOLE numeral on $5/$10/$20 bills, building the same total two ways, and comparing values to surface the front-digit misconception (saying $5 > $20 because '5 > 2').
student_learning_goal: I can identify bills up to $20.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can identify bills up to $20.
header.character_watermark: Coin Cassie the Cashier in the top-right with bill stack and cash register. Small (~1.5in). References blueprint.recurring_characters.

parts.student_instructions: Look at each bill. Write its VALUE in dollars. Read the WHOLE number, not just the front digit.
parts.visual_layout: Three bills shown ($5, $10, $20) with a blank line under each for the dollar value. Each bill has the numeral clearly visible. A small reminder at top: 'NUMBER says VALUE.'

image_placeholders.description: A Grade 1 bill-colour match for money worksheet, B&W line art. Left: $5, $10, $20 bills. Right: BLUE, PURPLE, GREEN colour labels.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: WS03_P1_COLOUR at Part 1: keywords name the bills colours match task.

parts.answer_key: $5 → 5 dollars; $10 → 10 dollars; $20 → 20 dollars. Watch for front-digit error ($20 → 'two').

parts.part_title: Part 2: Build the same VALUE two ways.
parts.student_instructions: Penny needs $10. Show TWO different ways to build $10 using bills. Draw or circle which bills.
parts.visual_layout: Two boxes labelled 'Way 1' and 'Way 2' with empty bill outlines. A bank of bill icons ($5, $10) at the bottom for reference. Penny says: 'Same VALUE, different ways!'

image_placeholders.description: A Grade 1 bill-value match for money worksheet, B&W line art. Left: 3 bills. Right: $5, $10, $20.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: WS03_P2_VALUES at Part 2: keywords name the bills values match task.

parts.answer_key: Way 1: one $10 bill. Way 2: two $5 bills. Both make $10.

parts.student_instructions: Look at each pair. Circle the bill (or set of bills) with the HIGHER value. Read the whole number first.
parts.visual_layout: Three rows: (a) $5 bill vs $20 bill, (b) two $5 bills vs one $20 bill, (c) three $5 bills vs one $10 bill. Each row has a YES/NO option for circling. Watch the front-digit trap: a child might choose $5 over $20 because '5 > 2'.

image_placeholders.description: A Grade 1 bill sort for money worksheet, B&W line art. 6 mixed bills at top. 3 bins at bottom: BLUE, PURPLE, GREEN.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: WS03_P3_SORT at Part 3: keywords name the bills bins sort task.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, draw the $20 bill from memory.
teacher_notes: Watch for the front-digit error in Part 3 — children choose $5 over $20 because '5 > 2'. Refer to expanded_walkthrough Diagnostic A for recovery: drill reading the WHOLE numeral aloud. Part 2 is the compose-two-ways task that anchors equivalent-value reasoning.
